paper.paper_scope: Review of strategies for developing lightweight (low-density) steels with focus on bulk ferrous alloys: classification by phase constitution (ferritic, austenitic, duplex, triplex), metallurgy, strengthening and ductility-enhancing mechanisms (precipitation hardening, solid-solution strengthening, TRIP, TWIP, SIP, MBIP), mechanical properties, processing routes, and application prospects versus traditional automotive steels.
paper.title: Overview of Lightweight Ferrous Materials: Strategies and Promises

unmapped_findings: The review classifies low-density bulk steels into four phase-constitution groups: ferritic (alpha), austenitic (gamma), duplex (alpha+gamma), and triplex (alpha+gamma+kappa-carbide).

Density-reduction strategies beyond bulk alloys include steel-based composites (ceramic-particle reinforced steel matrix), steel foams (75-95% porosity), and steel-based laminates; these are introduced but are not the main focus of the review.

General processing routes for low-density bulk steels are described in Fig. 13: hot rolling, coiling (about 650 C for Fe-Al IF-type alloys, 400 C for lean Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys, room-temperature coiling for rich Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys), cold rolling up to 66.67% thickness reduction, warm rolling for steels with Al > 8 wt.%, continuous annealing around 800-850 C, and low-temperature overaging around 400-450 C.
The alloy series Fe-30Mn-xAl-1C and Fe-xMn-7Al-1C (Fig. 7) are used to illustrate the alloying effect of Al and Mn on the kappa-carbide solvus, with x denoting variable Al or Mn amounts.

The paper also discusses standard automotive steels (IF-Rephos, ULC-BH340, HSLA350, DP500/600/800, TRIP600/780) in Table II for comparison, but these are conventional reference grades rather than the lightweight steels under study.
